status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1), approved 2025-07-04, added section 168(n) to the tax code through its section 70307, allowing a 100 percent depreciation deduction for qualified production property: the portion of nonresidential real property used as an integral part of manufacturing, production or refining, with construction beginning after 2025-01-19 and before 2029-01-01 and placed in service in the United States or a territory after 2025-07-04 and before 2031-01-01. IRS Notice 2026-16 gives interim guidance and invited comments by 2026-04-20; it sets no China-specific or relocation condition. Separately, Proclamation 11020, signed 2026-04-02 and published 2026-04-09, sets a 20 percent rate (rising to 100 percent on 2030-04-02) for companies with approved onshoring plans, effective 2026-07-31 for listed companies and 2026-09-29 for others, but it is a tariff measure covering all source countries. Proclamation 11045 (signed 2026-07-20) similarly halves the Section 232 aluminum duty for companies with approved plans to build or expand U.S. primary aluminum capacity, also without a China condition.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1) was approved; its section 70307 adds a 100 percent depreciation allowance for qualified production property placed in service in the United States.
Proclamation 11020 was published, setting a 20 percent pharmaceutical duty rate (rising to 100 percent in 2030) for companies with approved onshoring plans.

Proclamation 11045, Further Strengthening Actions Taken To Adjust Imports of Aluminum Into the United States, was signed (published 2026-07-23, 91 FR 46635); companies with Commerce-approved onshoring plans that commit to build, refurbish or expand a U.S. primary aluminum facility, with construction starting by 2029-01-20, may import primary aluminum at half the applicable Section 232 duty. The text does not mention China or relocation from China.
